newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: NATIONAL PARTY CONFUSED OVER LEADER'S REPUBLICAN STANCE
National Party Senate leader, Ron Boswell, says National Party leader, Tim Fischer wasn't helpful by floating a suggestion for a republic last week.

Senator Boswell says it's caused confusion among grass roots National Party members and hasn't been put to National Party MPs. He denies his comments are an attack on Mr Fischer, and says he is simply clarifying party policy, which is that there should be no change to the consitution.
AUSTRALIANS JOIN PROTESTS AGAINST ANIMALS IN SPACE
Australian animal rights campaigners in Melbourne and Sydney have joined an international protest today, calling on the American and Russian governments to stop sending animals into space.
Protests are also being held in the UK, the Netherlands, Germany, and the US, to mark the return of two monkeys to earth in a Russian space capsule.
The Australian group Animal Liberation claims the monkeys, sent into space to test the effect of weightlessness on astronauts, have endured a fortnight of terror and pain.
CYCLONE RACHEL SLOWS, BUT WINDS STRONGER
Tropical Cyclone Rachel, off Western Australia's north-west, has slowed, although winds have intensified.
Winds at the centre of the cyclone are estimated at 200 kilometres an hour.
State Emergency Service Assistant Regional Manager, Robert Te, says Port Hedland should experience its strongest winds by midday, local time.

However, he says Rachel is expected to run along the coast and may not cross at all. A short time ago Rachel was estimated at 80 kilometres north of Port Hedland moving west-south-west, at 15 kilometres an hour.
Mr Te says damage so far has been minimal.
VANSTONE SAYS ABORIGINES NEED EMPLOYMENT ASSISTANCE
The Federal Government says the future for the employment of young indigenous Australians lies with the private sector, in remote and rural areas.
In a speech to the Young Liberals convention in Melbourne, Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone says Aborigines desperately need special attention and funding.
Senator Vanstone says the previous Labor Government spent a lot of money encouraging indigenous employment, but much of it went on public sector jobs which are now being reduced.
She says the private sector must work in partnership with Government programmes, and has backed a proposal to give indigenous Australians English language assistance for indigenous students.
MEATWORKERS WARN ABOUT VIABILITY OF INDUSTRY
The meatworkers union says the viability of the processing industry has been put under a cloud by foreign aid programs.
Queensland Northern District President, Les Day, says northern abattoirs are having trouble getting cattle to kill due to the growth in live cattle exports.
And he says they're being sent to potential competitors like Indonesia, which has a growing meat processing industry sponsored by the Australian Government.
WORLD JOCKEYS CHALLENGE CANCELLED
The Australian Jockey Club has announced that industrial action has forced the cancellation of the World Jockeys Challenge.
The series was to have provided a showcase for Australian riders competing against top jockeys from around the world in a series of events throughout the summer.
But in a statement released by the AJC after consultations with other clubs, AJC Chief Executive Tony King says it was felt it would be unfair to involve overseas guests in a domestic dispute.
King cites statements from the National Jockeys Council that further industrial action could be taken in support of a pay claim, as evidence that the success of the Challenge could not be guaranteed.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
